# AF 第二章 原文（重制基线）

## Chapter 2

[P01] Three nights later old Major died quietly in his sleep. They buried him at the foot of the orchard（果园）. This was early in March. In the next three months, the animals did a lot of secret work. Major's speech gave the clever animals a whole new idea about life. They did not know when the uprising（起义） would happen, but they knew they must get ready for it. The pigs, the cleverest animals, taught and organised the others.

[P02] Among the pigs, two young boars（公猪） were the most important: Snowball and Napoleon. Mr. Jones was raising them to sell. Napoleon was a big, fierce Berkshire（伯克郡） boar（公猪）, the only one on the farm. He did not talk much, but he always got his own way. Snowball was more lively and had more new ideas, but people did not think he had the same deep character. The most famous of the other male（雄性） pigs was a small fat pig named Squealer. He had round cheeks, bright eyes, and a high, sharp（锋利） voice. He was a brilliant（聪明的） talker. When he argued a difficult point, he would jump from side to side and move his tail, and somehow（不知怎的） this made people believe him.

[P03] The others said that Squealer could turn black into white. These three pigs took old Major's teachings（教导） and made them into a complete system of thought, and they called it Animalism（动物主义）. Several nights a week, after Mr. Jones was asleep, they held secret meetings in the barn（谷仓） and explained the principles（原则） of Animalism to the others.

[P04] At first many animals were stupid and did not care. Some said they must be loyal（忠诚） to Mr. Jones and called him "Master." They said, "Mr. Jones feeds us. If he were gone, we would starve（饿死）." Others asked, "Why care what happens after we die?" or "If this uprising will happen anyway, does it matter if we work for it?" The pigs had a hard time showing them this was against Animalism. The stupidest questions came from Mollie, the white mare（母马）.

[P05] The first question she asked Snowball was: "Will there still be sugar after the uprising?" "No," said Snowball. "We cannot make sugar here. You will have all the oats（燕麦） and hay（干草） you want." "And can I still wear ribbons（丝带） in my mane（鬃毛）?" asked Mollie. "Comrade（同志）," said Snowball, "those ribbons are the badge（标志） of slavery. Is not freedom worth more than ribbons?" Mollie agreed, but she did not sound sure. The pigs had a harder time fighting the lies of Moses, the tame（驯服） raven（乌鸦）.

[P06] Moses was Mr. Jones's pet. He was a spy（间谍） and told tales, but he talked well. He said there was a secret place called Sugarcandy（糖块） Mountain. All animals went there when they died. It was up in the sky, a little above the clouds. There it was Sunday every day. Clover grew all year, and sugar and cake grew on the hedges（树篱）. The animals hated Moses because he told tales and did no work. But some believed in Sugarcandy Mountain. The pigs had to argue hard that it was not real.

[P07] These two were slow to think for themselves. But once they took the pigs as their teachers, they took in everything and passed it on in simple words. They never missed the secret meetings in the barn, and led the singing of 'animals of England'. Now the uprising came much earlier and more easily than anyone had thought. In past years, Mr. Jones was a hard master, but a good farmer. But later he lost money in a lawsuit（诉讼） and felt very sad. Then he began to drink too much.

[P08] He spent his days in a Windsor（温莎） chair in the kitchen. He read, drank, and sometimes fed Moses bread in beer. His men were idle（无所事事的） and dishonest（不诚实）. The fields were full of weeds（杂草）, and the buildings needed roofs. The animals did not have enough food. On Midsummer（仲夏）'s Eve（前夕）, Mr. Jones went to Willingdon. He got so drunk that he did not come back until midday（中午） on Sunday.

[P09] The men milked the cows early. Then they went to catch rabbits. They did not feed the animals. Mr. Jones came back and slept on the sofa. In the evening the animals still had no food. At last they could not wait. One cow broke the store-shed door with her horn. All the animals began to eat. Just then Mr. Jones woke up. He and his four men ran in with whips and hit out.

[P10] The hungry animals could not bear this. They all threw themselves at their tormentors（折磨者） together, though they had planned nothing before. Jones and his men were suddenly butted and kicked from every side. They could not control the situation. They had never seen animals act like this before. This sudden uprising of animals they were used to beating and treating badly scared them almost out of their wits（智慧）. After a moment or two they stopped trying to defend（保卫） themselves and ran away. A minute later all five were running fast down the cart-track to the main road, with the animals chasing（追赶） them in triumph（胜利）.

[P11] Jones looked out of the window and saw the animals. He quickly put some things in a bag and ran away by another way. Moses flew after him, croaking（呱呱叫） loudly. The animals had chased（追赶） Jones and his men onto the road and shut the gate. The uprising had worked: Jones was gone, and the farm was theirs. For the first few minutes the animals could hardly believe their good luck. They ran all around the farm to make sure no human was hiding there. Then they raced back to clean away the last signs of Jones's rule.

[P12] The room at the end of the stables was broken open. The bits, the nose-rings, the dog-chains, and the cruel knives were all thrown down the well. The reins（缰绳）, the halters（笼头）, the blinkers（眼罩）, and the nosebags（饲料袋） were thrown on the fire in the yard. So were the whips. All the animals jumped with joy when they saw the whips burning. Snowball also threw the ribbons on the fire. "Ribbons," he said, "should be considered as clothes, which are the mark of a human being.

[P13] All animals should go naked（裸体）." Boxer heard this and brought his small straw（稻草） hat. He threw it on the fire too. Soon the animals destroyed everything that reminded them of Mr. Jones. Napoleon led them back to the store-shed. He gave everyone a double ration（配给） of corn, and two biscuits for each dog. Then they sang 'Animals of England' seven times. After that they slept better than ever. But they woke at dawn（黎明） as usual. They remembered the great thing that had happened, and ran out into the pasture（牧场） together.

[P14] A little way down the pasture there was a small hill. From it they could see most of the farm. The animals ran to the top and looked around. Yes, it was theirs—everything they could see was theirs! They were so happy that they jumped and rolled in the wet grass. They ate mouthfuls（满口） of sweet summer grass. They kicked up the black earth and smelled its rich smell. Then they walked around the whole farm and looked at the fields, the hayfield（干草地）, the orchard, the pool, and the small wood.

[P15] They felt like they had never seen these things before. They could not believe it was all theirs. Then they walked back to the farm buildings and stood quietly outside the farmhouse（农舍） door. That was theirs too, but they were afraid to go in. After a moment, Snowball and Napoleon pushed the door open. The animals went in one by one, walking very carefully. They did not want to wake anything. They walked quietly from room to room. They were afraid to speak loudly. They looked with wonder at the rich things—the beds with soft feather（羽毛） mattresses（床垫）, the mirrors, the sofa, the carpet（地毯）, and the picture of Queen Victoria（维多利亚） above the fireplace（壁炉）.

[P16] They were coming down the stairs when they found Mollie was missing. They found her in the best bedroom. She had taken a blue ribbon（丝带） from Mrs. Jones's dressing-table. She held it against her shoulder and looked at herself in the glass in a foolish way. The others told her off sharply（尖锐地）, and they went outside. Some hams in the kitchen were taken out for burial（埋葬）. Boxer kicked the barrel（桶） of beer in the scullery（洗碗间） with his hoof（蹄） and broke it. Nothing else in the house was touched. They all agreed that the farmhouse should be kept as a museum.

[P17] All agreed that no animal must ever live there. Then the animals had breakfast. After that, Snowball and Napoleon called them together again. "Comrades（同志们）," said Snowball, "it is half-past six and we have a long day. Today we begin the hay harvest. But first we must do another thing." The pigs then showed that in the past three months they had taught themselves to read and write. They learned from an old spelling book. It had belonged to Mr. Jones's children and was thrown on the rubbish heap（堆）.

[P18] Napoleon sent for black and white paint. He led the way to the big gate. Snowball was best at writing. He painted out FARM on the top bar（酒吧）. In its place he painted ANIMAL FARM. That was the farm's name from then on. Then they went back. Snowball and Napoleon set a ladder against the big barn's end wall. The pigs had studied for three months. They had put Animalism into Seven Commandments（戒律）.

[P19] The Seven Commandments would now be written on the wall as a law all animals on Animal Farm must obey for ever. Snowball climbed a ladder and worked. Squealer held the paint-pot below him. The words were written in big white letters. Animals could read them from thirty yards away. They said: THE SEVEN COMMANDMENTS 1. Whatever goes on two legs is an enemy. Whatever goes on four legs, or has wings, is a friend.

[P20] No animal shall wear clothes. No animal shall sleep in a bed. No animal shall drink alcohol（酒精）. No animal shall kill another animal. All animals are equal. It was written neatly（整洁地）, and the spelling was mostly right. Snowball read it aloud. All the animals nodded, and the clever ones began to learn the Commandments by heart. "Now, comrades," cried Snowball, throwing down the paint-brush, "to the hayfield! Let us get in the harvest more quickly than Jones and his men could do." But then the three cows, who had seemed uneasy（不安） for some time, set up a loud lowing.

[P21] The cows had not been milked for twenty-four hours, and their udders（乳房） were almost bursting（爆裂）. The pigs sent for buckets and milked them well. Soon there were five buckets of frothing milk. Many animals looked at it with great interest. "What will happen to all that milk?" said someone. "Jones sometimes mixed some in our mash（糊状饲料）," said a hen. "Never mind the milk, comrades!" cried Napoleon. "That will be attended to. The harvest is more important. Comrade Snowball will lead the way.

[P22] "I will come soon. Go forward, comrades! The hay is waiting." So the animals went to work. When they came back, the milk was gone.
